subject: Urgent: Pinnacle Retail ingest failures — client header trimming causing p99 latency & 500s
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie@pinnacleretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Chu <ben.chu@pinnacleretail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production alerts — checkout streaming errors up 3x

Logan —

We're seeing a large uptick in 500s and p99 latency on our checkout live stream starting ~08:45 PT. Error rate is about 3.2% (normally <0.2%). Revenue impact is visible.

What we see in our logs: repeated parser errors like "incomplete header: expected 128 bytes, got 78" and then a connection reset. It correlates with our client SDK (v1.4.7) rollout at 07:30. Rolling back the SDK to 1.4.6 reduces the errors immediately.

We need urgent help — can you confirm if this sounds like a Redwood-side issue or the SDK? We're open to a joint call.

Attachments: pnr_debug_1218.tar.gz (text/plain) — contains sample request traces and server logs.

—Natalie
Site Reliability Lead, Pinnacle Retail
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Park <natalie@pinnacleretail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production alerts — checkout streaming errors up 3x

Grace / Karthik / Marissa —

FYI from Pinnacle: spike in parser errors and p99 latency that coincides with their rollout of client-sdk v1.4.7. They report immediate improvement after rolling back to 1.4.6. Sample logs attached (pnr_debug_1218.tar.gz).

Initial ask: Can eng reproduce quickly and confirm whether our server-side parsing tolerates trimmed/malformed last-header chunks? If this is a client SDK change that trims trailing header bytes under some batching conditions, we need a mitigation ASAP (either a temporary runtime tolerant mode or a coordination with the client to force-backwards).

Proposed immediate actions:
- Grace: triage and confirm root cause (server vs client) within 60 minutes.
- Karthik: support with any config toggle to accept partial headers or to fail-open for that route.
- Marissa: should we mobilize PNR exec contact and offer credits / mitigation?

I'm standing by for updates and can jump on a call with Pinnacle.

—Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Park <natalie@pinnacleretail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:49:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production alerts — checkout streaming errors up 3x

Logan / Karthik —

Quick triage notes (repro'd in the staging harness with PNR traces):
- Symptom: client SDK sometimes strips the final header segment when batching small frames; server streaming parser expects a header-length prefix that then points to the header bytes. If the last chunk is shortened, the parser hits a length mismatch error and tears down the connection. That matches the "expected X got Y" errors in PNR logs.
- When we replay identical traffic with SDK v1.4.6, the frames arrive intact; v1.4.7 introduces an opportunistic coalescing optimization that can drop padding bytes in the last chunk when the request fits a micro-batch.

Immediate mitigation we can deploy from our side: enable parser tolerance flag to accept partial header payloads and attempt reassembly across the next N frames (configurable; default N=1). Risk: slightly higher CPU while reassembling and possible token duplication in worst-case.

Workaround on customer side: roll back to 1.4.6 (they already tried this) OR set their SDK env var REDWOOD_DISABLE_COALESCE=1 which prevents the micro-coalesce behavior.

I'll prepare a minimal server patch to turn on tolerant reassembly for the Pinnacle routes and push to prod as a canary. ETA ~2 hours for the canary and 4 hours for global rollout assuming no regression.

Attachments: client-sdk-1.4.7-diff.patch (text/plain) — patch summary of the coalescing change.

—Grace
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Ben Chu <ben.chu@pinnacleretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production alerts — checkout streaming errors up 3x

Thanks for the quick analysis. Our finance team is already seeing cart abandonment at scale. If you can push a server-side tolerance flag as an immediate mitigation that's ideal. We'll keep the rollback in flight as a safety valve.

Also: what's the ETA for a permanent fix? We need a timeline before our execs escalate.

—Ben
Engineering Manager, Pinnacle Retail
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Park <natalie@pinnacleretail.com>, Ben Chu <ben.chu@pinnacleretail.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 07:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec briefing: Pinnacle Retail production incident (parser header trimming)

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick exec summary for awareness and any escalation:
- Impact: Pinnacle reported 3.2% error rate on checkout streams (from 0.2%), measurable revenue impact.
- Root cause (prelim): client-sdk v1.4.7 introduced micro-batching/coalescing that can drop trailing header bytes in small frames; Redwood streaming parser is strict and errors out on length mismatch.
- Immediate mitigation: Grace will push a parser-tolerance flag to Pinnacle's routes as a canary (ETA 2 hours). Customer can roll back SDK (they have) or set env var to disable coalescing.
- Permanent fix options: (A) server tolerant reassembly + smarter deduping (low effort, medium risk), (B) force strictness and require client SDK rollback / patch (low risk, longer customer pain), (C) patch client SDK to change coalescing behavior (we should coordinate release cadence).

Action items requested from leadership:
1) Decision on compensation/credits threshold if we keep Paxil (Pinnacle) in degraded state beyond 12 hours.
2) Approve priority for a hotfix (Grace's server patch) and an expedited client SDK patch release.
3) Authorize an on-call rotation to monitor the canary (Grace + one SRE).

I'll mark this as P0 and stay on the thread.

—Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Park <natalie@pinnacleretail.com>, Ben Chu <ben.chu@pinnacleretail.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 16:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Resolution: Pinnacle routing patch deployed + next steps

Update — final resolution and follow-up plan:
- Deployed tolerant-reassembly patch as a canary to 10% of PNR traffic at 14:10 PT on 2026-12-20; error rate dropped to baseline in the canary fleet within ~7 minutes. Rolled to 100% at 15:05 PT.
- Customer rollback remained in place for a 60-minute buffer window; we coordinated a joint verification run with PNR and confirmed full recovery.
- Root cause confirmed: client-sdk 1.4.7 micro-coalesce optimization that removed trailing header padding under certain micro-batch sizes.

Immediate follow-up deliverables:
1) Engineering: ship a non-invasive server-side reassembly improvement (postmortem + PR) to make parsers resilient without significant CPU overhead. ETA: 7 days.
2) SDK team: patch v1.4.8 to remove the problematic coalesce behaviour or gate it behind an opt-in flag. ETA: 3 days.
3) Customer ops: Logan to propose a goodwill credit (TBD) and coordinate a stakeholder readout 12/21.

Attach: postmortem-draft-20261220.md (text/plain). Will iterate on that doc and loop legal if credits > $X.

—Grace
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
